recognize_zh: 臨床照片顯示下肢皮膚有數處邊界模糊的紫藍至黃綠色瘀青（ecchymoses），沒有點狀出血或明顯腫脹；在類澱粉沉積症合併後天性凝血因子 X 缺乏的病人，這類皮下出血是凝血因子缺乏型出血的表現，但照片本身無法確立病因。
features: Clinical photograph of a lower extremity with several poorly demarcated ecchymoses
Central violaceous-blue bruise with surrounding yellow-green discoloration indicating resolving hemorrhage
Additional faint purplish bruising on the proximal portion of the limb
No petechiae, palpable purpura, or hemarthrosis-type swelling evident
Overlying skin otherwise intact without ulceration
describe_en: Clinical photograph of the lower extremity shows several poorly demarcated ecchymoses with a central violaceous area and surrounding yellow-green discoloration, indicating hemorrhages of different ages. No petechiae, palpable purpura, or skin necrosis is seen. Superficial ecchymoses without petechiae favor a coagulation factor or vascular fragility defect over thrombocytopenia. In a patient with systemic AL amyloidosis, the appearance is compatible with bleeding from acquired factor X deficiency, which must be confirmed by prolonged PT and aPTT with a low factor X activity.

ddx.vs: Thrombocytopenic bleeding typically produces petechiae and mucosal bleeding, and platelet count would be low, whereas this image shows ecchymoses without petechiae.

ddx.dx: Anticoagulant or vitamin K deficiency coagulopathy
ddx.vs: These cause similar ecchymoses but show deficiency of multiple vitamin K-dependent factors correctable by vitamin K, rather than isolated factor X deficiency.
Acquired hemophilia causes extensive soft-tissue ecchymoses with an isolated prolonged aPTT and factor VIII inhibitor, with a normal PT.

ddx.dx: Senile purpura or amyloid vascular fragility
ddx.vs: Vascular fragility purpura occurs with normal coagulation studies and, in amyloidosis, often appears as periorbital pinch purpura.
